tweet.text:
I go through phases with a project.  
1. Lots of features given to the specifier of the swarm.  The swarm builds and verifies with all the constraints and tools.  Very productive and safe, but slower than raw vibe coding.
2. Single agent tweaking, especially of the UI.  Very fast turnaround that tweaking requires.  This is as close to vibe coding as I get.
3. Robustness run.  After the tweaks I run through all the crap, dry, mutate wringer.  It takes awhile.  Good for a lunch break or the last prompt of the day.
4. Tune the swarm.  As the project grows things slow down.  So I increase the emphasis on differential mutation, and other slow operations.  This tuning can take hours.
5. Architectural review.  Module structure, partitioning, dependencies, etc.  I have the swarm do this, but I'm prompting the architect rather than the specifier.  This restructuring can take hours.
Go to 1.

So it's an interesting oscillation between feature growth and hardening.  Big spurts of features for a few days followed by a day of hardening.
